name: moderation-notice
title: Moderation notice
description: What a player is told, and what they can do about somebody else. Two treatments on `data-gs-presentation`. The notice names the cause and the next action, with no apology, no "something went wrong" and above all no silence, because a player whose message vanishes without a word learns only that the room is broken; `refused` did not post and `held` still might, and the two are drawn differently so a hold is not read as a refusal. The menu is three worded entries at 48px each, never a row of bare icons where report and block are one slip apart, and the block entry says what the player gets rather than what happens to the other person. A report changes nothing on screen, so the room cannot work out who reported. Decides nothing and sends nothing: the words naming the rule are the host's, and the way to the house rules is a node it passes rather than a link built from a prop.
docs: Pass `reason` with the words naming which house rule was broken. The default says only that one was, because the library does not know your rules, and a refusal that cannot say why is the dead end BDS-042 forbids. Pass `rules` as your own link element: the component builds no link target from a prop, the same boundary `sponsor` holds. Use `moderation="held"` while a person is still reading, and say so in that wording rather than in a refusal's, because it may still post. For the menu set `presentation="menu"` and give only the handlers you want entries for; each entry appears for its handler and no other way. Pass `author` and the block entry names them. Reporting is yours: confirm it somewhere else, such as a `toast`, and leave this on screen unchanged.
